content: Spouses married February 1997 under legal community property. Wife sought division of various assets including husband's stock options, Prometheia pension fund proceeds, and offsets for maintenance payments and household expenses. Husband contested, arguing stock options, pension fund proceeds, and various payments constituted personal property or non-recurring services. Articles 177(a)(c), 143, 147, 192, 2034 Italian Civil Code govern purchases during marriage, residual community, spousal contribution duty, and non-repetition of morally-obligated payments. Issues concerned whether credit rights (stock options) fall within community property, pension fund treatment under residual community, and whether maintenance/household payments deductible from division. Supreme Court established credit rights and complex rights (share rights) fall within community property as assets per Articles 810, 812, 813—legal community protection transcends asset nature and right character. Stock options constitute option rights to purchase shares—relative rights falling within Article 177(a) concept of purchase. Company shares subscribed exercising option rights constitute acquisitions within community property scope, even though financial aspect predominates over shareholder status rights. Holdings in plaintiff's account (€114,855.84) subject to division. Accenture stock options sale proceeds (€45,000) also divisible: plaintiff failed proving shares acquired pre-marriage or through donation/will/personal asset exchange—burden unmet, therefore community property. Prometheia pension fund (€87,802.31) falls within residual community per Article 177(c): pension benefits replace separate activity income, subject to community if existing at dissolution (separation filing June 2010). Maintenance payments (€900 monthly pre-presidential order) non-repetitive per Articles 143, 147 contribution duty—expression of primary family regime identical in both property regimes. Payment in fulfillment of legal obligation precludes repetition; Article 2034 bars recovery of morally-obligated transfers. Post-presidential order payments non-deductible: paid fulfilling legal obligation after community dissolution. Household expenses (rent, utilities, restoration) non-deductible: non-recurring services attributable to Article 143 contribution duty performed during marriage. Medical expenses (€6,221) non-deductible: mutual material assistance duty payments made pre-separation order. However, €18,000 advance payment on dissolution per private agreement deductible: atypical transaction expressing negotiating autonomy anticipating separation effects, valid unless detrimental or contrary to public policy. Movable property divided per court-appointed expert valuation: items in defendant's possession (€3,631 valued goods) assigned to her; remaining goods assigned to plaintiff proportionate to values.
